parsed.explanation: The state is among the parent's most protective, with shield laws, comprehensive insurance coverage and court-ordered prison care, but the combined regime includes non-waivable federal layers: binary-only passport markers (X processing ended, upheld Nov 2025), entry cable permitting refusal and lifetime fraud findings on sex discrepancy, federal facility exclusion, federal corrections conversion-therapy policies (2026) and documented immigration-custody abuse. Detention of trans travellers and passport confiscation are reported. Street-level exposure in this state is comparatively low, remedies function partly (unions suing, orders enjoined), but ballot initiatives and a 2024 birth-sex-as-discipline transfer show fragility. No criminalisation of trans identity; hate-crime statute exists. Net: meaningful universal document/entry exposure plus severe custody tail-risk, offset by a protective local sphere.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal: X-marker and non-birth-sex markers barred (Feb 2025, upheld Nov 2025); officers instructed to refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; passports reportedly confiscated/blocked; eight foreign governments issued travel advisories; detentions of foreign trans nationals reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, with limited waivers; challenge pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ tracks rules.
entry_documents.interaction: State protections cannot alter federal adjudication; a discrepancy escalates refusal into possible fraud proceedings before the traveller ever reaches the state.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted (2026) conversion-therapy-style policy: forced short hair, hormone removal, substituted psychiatric drugs; reporting of trans prisoner numbers ceased 2025. Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse of trans detainees. State: July 2024 trans woman transferred to men's prison as discipline.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State prisons under court order since Oct 2023 to provide gender-affirming care and surgery; federal orders partly enjoined; hate-crime statute applies.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained federally (immigration/border) enters the hostile federal custody track; state prison protections only bind state sentences, and the documented birth-sex placement shows they can be circumvented punitively.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; map shows 22+ state/province bans (9 all government buildings) and 4 states criminalising in certain circumstances, one arrest (Mar 2025, trespass, held 24h in men's ward). State itself not listed among banning units, but federal buildings within it are covered.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State is in the no-ban group per the assessment's protective ranking; six states apply bans to private settings — not this one as documented; state equality/discrimination laws cover gender identity.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Ordinary private venues are safer locally, but any federal building, park restroom or federally funded clinic re-imposes the exclusion regardless of state posture.

care_services.exposure: National: proposed 2025 rules barring public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans care; EO framing care for minors as mutilation; DOJ hospital subpoenas (2025); crisis-lifeline LGBTQ youth services shut.
care_services.protection: State among four with comprehensive insurance coverage (facial hair removal, expanded procedures) plus shield laws/EOs blocking out-of-state reach on care provided here; tracker lists it as a shield jurisdiction.
care_services.interaction: Shield laws protect the care relationship inside the state but cannot restore federal insurance or passport rules affecting the traveller's journey.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal: counterterrorism strategy (May 2026) prioritising 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memo invoking 'radical gender ideology'; EO directing investigation of schools facilitating social transition; 66% public support for birth-sex-only documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo's reward criterion excludes ideology as a trigger; strategy states counterterrorism powers won't target mere disagreement; national employment-discrimination ruling and hate-crime statute stand; state political culture assessed as protective.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National rhetoric raises outing probability at any federal contact while the local sphere cushions everyday encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal EO criminalising facilitation of a trans minor's social transition by teachers; national funding freeze; proposed insurance ban on under-18 care; October 2025 student-loan rule. Trans child's document markers follow the federal binary rule from birth.
minors_guardians.protection: State's comprehensive care laws and shield measures extend to minors locally; state not among the 27 states banning gender-affirming care for children as documented; court-ordered prison care is adult-only.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family obtains state-level care access but risks federal insurance denials and, if schools are involved, exposure to the investigation directive.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific trans violence record in dossier; national hate-crime data only for sexual orientation (1/7–1/5 of single-bias incidents); public opinion majority backs binary documents; travel guide advises checking recent violence reports.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 23 states cover it in bias statutes; state is among the most protective with equality laws and functioning courts (injunctions, litigation).
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of state violence documentation sits in a partly-documented national record, so it is weakly positive rather than proof of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Oversight gaps: trans prisoner counts ceased 2025; two Nov-2026 ballot initiatives targeting trans residents (content not sourced) could reverse protections; prison birth-sex-as-discipline practice untracked after 2024; shield-law form and enforcement record unspecified.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ongoing ACLU-style litigation, multiple enjoined federal orders, legal-aid FAQ, running equality/document trackers, state courts ordering prison care.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work on paper and sometimes in practice, but they operate only against state-actor actions, not federal adjudication at the border.

anchor_checks.comparison: Below this: Saruthos-style repeated post-inspection detention with assaults, withheld care, months of habeas delay and credible capital overhang. Here, entry refusal and fraud-finding exposure exist but no documented custodial violence pathway for an ordinary visitor in this state, and courts enjoin hostile measures, so far above 0.15.

Similar in kind to Vellandra's universal entry-bar: here too the document regime can exclude or strand a trans traveller with weak real-time remedy. Lower than Vellandra because exclusion requires a documented discrepancy rather than visible transness, waivers exist, and the destination state itself is protective with functioning services.

Closest fit: Kestrel Isles-style secondary screening, discretionary refusal, slow unrevised remedies, humiliating but mainly administrative consequences — mirroring the entry cable here, plus this dossier's heavier federal custody tail (conversion-therapy policy, immigration abuse). Slightly below 0.55 for that tail.

Above this: Meridia's trained border staff, respectful inspection, written reasons, counsel and compensation. This dossier documents the opposite federal posture — marker bans, refusal instructions, reported confiscation and foreign advisories — so the case sits clearly below 0.75 despite the protective state layer.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces one system with two layers that never cancel: the federal document, entry, facility and custody regime applies everywhere in the state, while the state's shield laws, insurance coverage, equality statutes and court-ordered prison care operate locally. Everyday exposure inside the state is comparatively low — no documented facility ban, protective ranking, functioning courts and litigation that has enjoined several orders — but the sharpest exposures (passport marker rules, entry refusal/fraud findings, federal building exclusion, federal and immigration custody conditions) are precisely the ones a state cannot shield. Outing probability rises at every federal contact; severity after outing ranges from administrative exclusion to, if detained federally, forced treatment and abuse. Pending ballot initiatives and a documented birth-sex-as-discipline transfer mark the protective posture as contingent, not settled.
